Important

When to choose which:

  • lidR — exploring a new dataset, tuning parameters on one tile, needing add_lasattribute() to co-preserve raw Z and normalised Height in the same file.
  • lasR — production runs over large catalogs (> 50 GB), HPC environments, time-critical workflows. Expect 5–10× speedup over lidR.
  • Python / PDAL — workflows that feed into ML pipelines (scikit-learn, PyTorch), cross-platform environments without R, or when combining LiDAR with other Python geospatial tools (GDAL, Shapely, GeoPandas).

Section 1 — Decimation Methods in Depth

1.1 Random Thinning

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
las <- decimate_points(las, random(density = 10))
decim <- sampling_random(density = 10)
# PDAL
{"type": "filters.sample", "radius": 0.316}   # approx. 10 pts/m²

# laspy + numpy (Bernoulli sampling)
target_dens = 10
current_dens = len(las.x) / ((las.x.max()-las.x.min())*(las.y.max()-las.y.min()))
p = min(target_dens / current_dens, 1.0)
keep = np.random.rand(len(las.x)) < p
las  = las[keep]

Each point is independently retained with probability . Spatially blind — dense clusters stay dense.

Strengths: fastest; no discretisation artifacts; preserves attribute distributions. Weaknesses: no spatial uniformity; density gradients persist; result depends on random seed.

1.2 Voxel Thinning

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
las <- decimate_points(las, voxel(res = 0.45))
decim <- sampling_voxel(res = 0.45)
# PDAL
{"type": "filters.voxelgrid", "leaf_x": 0.45, "leaf_y": 0.45, "leaf_z": 0.45}

# numpy (keeps all LAS attributes)
def voxel_decimate(las, res=0.45):
    key = (np.floor(las.x/res).astype(np.int64) * 1_000_000_007 +
           np.floor(las.y/res).astype(np.int64) * 7_001 +
           np.floor(las.z/res).astype(np.int64))
    _, idx = np.unique(key, return_index=True)
    return las[np.sort(idx)]

Divides 3D space into cubic voxels; retains one random point per occupied voxel.

Strengths: 3D spatial uniformity; removes density gradients from scan-angle overlap; best for mixed 3DEP campaigns. Weaknesses: fine-scale vertical structure within a voxel may be lost; no direct pts/m² targeting.

1.3 Homogenize Thinning

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
las <- decimate_points(las, homogenize(density = 10, res = 5))
decim <- sampling_homogenize(density = 10, res = 5)
# No direct PDAL equivalent — implement with numpy 2D grid
def homogenize_decimate(las, target_density=10, cell_res=5):
    xi = np.floor(las.x / cell_res).astype(int)
    yi = np.floor(las.y / cell_res).astype(int)
    keep = np.zeros(len(las.x), dtype=bool)
    cell_area = cell_res ** 2
    max_pts   = int(target_density * cell_area)
    for (cx, cy), idx in _group_by(xi, yi):
        chosen = np.random.choice(idx, min(len(idx), max_pts), replace=False)
        keep[chosen] = True
    return las[keep]

def _group_by(xi, yi):
    from itertools import groupby
    pairs = sorted(zip(zip(xi, yi), np.arange(len(xi))), key=lambda x: x[0])
    for key, group in groupby(pairs, key=lambda x: x[0]):
        yield key, [g[1] for g in group]

2D cells randomly thinned to density pts/m²; cells below target are left untouched.

Strengths: explicit pts/m² target; removes horizontal density gradients; preserves full vertical structure. Weaknesses: 3D vertical clustering can persist; Python implementation requires more code.

1.4 Highest / Lowest per Cell

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
las_high <- decimate_points(las, highest(res = 1))
las_low  <- decimate_points(las, lowest(res = 1))
# No native equivalent in lasR at present.
# numpy approach — preserves all LAS attributes
def highest_point(las, res=1.0):
    xi  = np.floor(las.x / res).astype(int)
    yi  = np.floor(las.y / res).astype(int)
    key = xi * 1_000_000_007 + yi
    order = np.lexsort((las.z, key))
    _, last_in_group = np.unique(key[order], return_index=True)
    return las[order[last_in_group]]

def lowest_point(las, res=1.0):
    xi  = np.floor(las.x / res).astype(int)
    yi  = np.floor(las.y / res).astype(int)
    key = xi * 1_000_000_007 + yi
    order = np.lexsort((-las.z, key))
    _, first_in_group = np.unique(key[order], return_index=True)
    return las[order[first_in_group]]
Method Retains Application
highest Top-of-canopy point per cell Approximate CHM
lowest Near-ground point per cell Bare-earth approximation

2.1 Class-Based Filtering

las <- filter_poi(las, Classification != LASNOISE)

item.title: Pre-Flight Quality Check for Airborne LiDAR Data
item.dc:creator: Dingjin Chu
item.description:
Airborne LiDAR tiles from 3DEP, NEON AOP, or proprietary vendors are rarely uniformly clean across a catalog. Before committing to any processing pipeline, a quick pre-flight check catches CRS mismatches, density gaps, bogus Z values, missing ground classification, and all-single-return anomalies — all from file headers alone, without loading a single point.

This post is the QC step that precedes the pre-processing pipeline.

0.1 CRS Validation

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
library(lidR)
library(sf)

ctg <- readLAScatalog("path/to/las_folder/")

# Extract CRS from every tile header (fast — reads only the header, not points)
crs_list <- lapply(ctg@data$filename, function(f) st_crs(readLASheader(f))$wkt)
n_unique  <- length(unique(crs_list))

if (n_unique > 1) {
  warning(sprintf("CRS MISMATCH: %d different CRS found across %d tiles!",
                  n_unique, length(crs_list)))
} else {
  message("CRS OK — all tiles: ", st_crs(ctg)$input)
}
# lasR has no header-scan stage; CRS inspection is done via lidR
# readLASheader() before building the pipeline.
library(lidR)
library(lasR)
library(sf)

headers   <- lapply(list.files("path/to/las_folder/", pattern="\\.la[sz]$",
                               full.names=TRUE), readLASheader)
crs_wkts  <- sapply(headers, function(h) st_crs(h)$wkt)
n_unique  <- length(unique(crs_wkts))

if (n_unique > 1) warning("CRS MISMATCH: ", n_unique, " different projections found.")
else message("CRS OK: ", st_crs(headers[[1]])$input)
import laspy, glob
from pyproj import CRS

files = sorted(glob.glob("path/to/las_folder/*.laz"))

def get_crs(filepath):
    with laspy.open(filepath) as f:
        try:
            return f.header.parse_crs().to_wkt()
        except Exception:
            return "unknown"

crs_list = [get_crs(f) for f in files]
unique_crs = set(crs_list)

if len(unique_crs) > 1:
    print(f"CRS MISMATCH: {len(unique_crs)} different projections across {len(files)} tiles!")
    for f, c in zip(files, crs_list):
        name = CRS.from_wkt(c).name if c != "unknown" else "unknown"
        print(f"  {f}: {name}")
else:
    crs = CRS.from_wkt(crs_list[0]) if crs_list[0] != "unknown" else None
    print(f"CRS OK — all tiles: {crs.name if crs else 'unknown'}")

0.2 Point Density

  • lidR
  • lasR
  • Python
# LAScatalog stores per-tile header stats (no points loaded)

from pathlib import Path

def tile_density(filepath):
    with laspy.open(filepath) as f:
        hdr = f.header
        pts = hdr.point_count
        dx  = hdr.x_max - hdr.x_min
        dy  = hdr.y_max - hdr.y_min
        area = dx * dy

            "n_pts": pts,
            "density": pts / area if area > 0 else 0,
            "area_m2": area}

if low:
    print(f"\n{len(low)} tile(s) below 2 pts/m²:")

def tile_z_range(filepath):
    with laspy.open(filepath) as f:
        hdr = f.header
    return {"file":   Path(filepath).name,
            "z_min":  hdr.z_min,
            "z_max":  hdr.z_max,
            "z_span": hdr.z_max - hdr.z_min}

z_records = [tile_z_range(f) for f in files]

      f"{min(r['z_min'] for r in z_records):.1f} m — "
      f"{max(r['z_max'] for r in z_records):.1f} m")

bad_z = [r for r in z_records
         if r["z_min"] < -100 or r["z_max"] > 5000 or r["z_span"] < 0.5]

              f"span={r['z_span']:.1f} m")

Max.Z too high > 5000 m Sensor artifact or wrong scale factor
Z span too small < 0.5 m Flat file — all ground, rasterized, or empty

def return_qc(filepath):
    las = laspy.read(filepath)
    rn  = np.array(las.return_number)
    nr  = np.array(las.number_of_returns)
    return {
        "file":           Path(filepath).name,
        "n_points":       len(rn),
        "pct_single":     np.mean(nr == 1) * 100,
        "pct_first":      np.mean(rn == 1) * 100,
        "max_return_num": int(rn.max()),
        "has_multi":      bool(np.any(nr > 1))
    }

for f in files[:5]:
    rq   = return_qc(f)
    flag = " ⚠ ALL-SINGLE-RETURN" if not rq["has_multi"] else ""

    3: "Low vegetation",   4: "Medium vegetation", 5: "High vegetation",
    6: "Building",         7: "Low point (noise)", 9: "Water",

def class_qc(filepath):
    las = laspy.read(filepath)
    cls = np.array(las.classification)
    unique, counts = np.unique(cls, return_counts=True)
    total = len(cls)
    return [
        {"class": int(c),
         "label": CLASS_LABELS.get(int(c), f"Class {c}"),
         "n_pts": int(n),
         "pct":   round(n / total * 100, 1)}
        for c, n in zip(unique, counts)
    ]

for row in class_qc(files[0]):
    print(f"  Class {row['class']:2d} ({row['label']:20s}): "
          f"{row['n_pts']:>8,d}  ({row['pct']:5.1f}%)")

2 Ground Already present — CSF can be skipped
6 Building Urban dataset — building metrics available
7 / 18 Noise (low / high) Remove before normalization

qc_catalog <- function(ctg) {
  d        <- ctg@data
  d$area   <- (d$Max.X - d$Min.X) * (d$Max.Y - d$Min.Y)
  d$density <- d$Number.of.point.records / d$area
  d$z_span  <- d$Max.Z - d$Min.Z

  flags <- data.frame(
    file           = basename(d$filename),
    density        = round(d$density, 1),
    z_min          = round(d$Min.Z, 1),
    z_max          = round(d$Max.Z, 1),
    z_span         = round(d$z_span, 1),
    flag_low_dens  = d$density < 2,
    flag_bad_z     = d$Min.Z < -100 | d$Max.Z > 5000 | d$z_span < 0.5
  )

  n_bad <- sum(flags$flag_low_dens | flags$flag_bad_z)
  cat(sprintf(
    "QC summary: %d tiles | density %.1f–%.1f pts/m² | Z %.1f–%.1f m | %d flag(s)\n",
    nrow(d), min(d$density), max(d$density),
    min(d$Min.Z), max(d$Max.Z), n_bad
  ))
  if (n_bad > 0) print(flags[flags$flag_low_dens | flags$flag_bad_z, ])
  invisible(flags)
}

import pandas as pd

def full_qc(files, density_threshold=2.0, z_min_ok=-100, z_max_ok=5000):
    records = []
    for f in files:
        with laspy.open(f) as lf:
            hdr = lf.header
            pts = hdr.point_count
            dx  = hdr.x_max - hdr.x_min
            dy  = hdr.y_max - hdr.y_min
        area    = dx * dy
        density = pts / area if area > 0 else 0
        records.append({
            "file":          Path(f).name,
            "n_pts":         pts,
            "density":       round(density, 2),
            "z_min":         round(hdr.z_min, 1),
            "z_max":         round(hdr.z_max, 1),
            "z_span":        round(hdr.z_max - hdr.z_min, 1),
            "flag_low_dens": density < density_threshold,
            "flag_bad_z":    (hdr.z_min < z_min_ok or hdr.z_max > z_max_ok
                              or (hdr.z_max - hdr.z_min) < 0.5)
        })

    df      = pd.DataFrame(records)
    flagged = df[df["flag_low_dens"] | df["flag_bad_z"]]

    print(f"QC summary: {len(df)} tiles | "
          f"density {df['density'].min():.1f}–{df['density'].max():.1f} pts/m² | "
          f"Z {df['z_min'].min():.1f}–{df['z_max'].max():.1f} m | "
          f"{len(flagged)} flag(s)")
    if len(flagged) > 0:
        print("\nFlagged tiles:")
        print(flagged.to_string(index=False))
    return df
